metadata.title: 1983 Case 45
metadata.original_presentation: A 31-year-old man was admitted to the hospital because of chest pain and a mass in the anterior thoracic wall.

required.content: What is the patient's history of present illness?
required.response: The patient experienced left anterior chest pain 3 1/2 months ago, was diagnosed with pleurisy, and prescribed ibuprofen. He later developed night sweats, chills, feverish sensation, and a mass in the left anterior chest wall.

teaching_points.content: Pleurisy can present with chest pain and may be associated with other systemic symptoms.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical and social history?
required.response: The patient worked cleaning boiler rooms, smoked two packs of cigarettes daily for 10 years, drank alcohol in moderation, and smoked marijuana. He has a family history of malignant tumors.

teaching_points.content: Occupational exposure and smoking history are important risk factors for respiratory and systemic diseases.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lung Cancer with Chest Wall Involvement
Tuberculosis
refuting_evidence: mass in anterior thoracic wall is less typical

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pleurisy
refuting_evidence: development of mass in anterior thoracic wall
systemic symptoms like night sweats and chills
additional_information_needed: evaluation of pleural fluid if present

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lymphoma
refuting_evidence: smoking history more suggestive of lung cancer
additional_information_needed: CT scan of chest and abdomen

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The patient appeared thin, with a very firm mass in the left pectoral region, diminished respiratory movement on the left side, and no rales. The rest of the examination was normal.

teaching_points.content: Physical examination can reveal important clues such as masses and respiratory changes that guide further investigation.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pancoast tumor
supporting_evidence: mass in the left anterior chest wall
refuting_evidence: mass location is anterior rather than apical
no mention of Horner's syndrome or arm pain

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Tuberculosis
key_features: mass could be a tuberculous abscess
refuting_evidence: mass is very firm rather than fluctuant

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lung cancer
refuting_evidence: mass is in the chest wall rather than lung parenchyma

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chest wall sarcoma
supporting_evidence: very firm mass in the left pectoral region
additional_information_needed: imaging studies to assess local invasion

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic pleuritis with effusion
refuting_evidence: very firm mass rather than fluid collection
no rales or signs of effusion
additional_information_needed: pleural fluid analysis if effusion is present

required.content: What were the results of the laboratory tests and imaging studies?
required.response: Hematocrit was 33.6%, WBC 13,700 with 75% neutrophils, ESR 115 mm/hr. Chest X-ray showed a density in the lingula, CT scan revealed a mass in the lingula extending into the mediastinum and thoracic wall.

teaching_points.content: Elevated ESR and WBC can indicate inflammation or infection. Imaging studies are crucial for assessing the extent of thoracic masses.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lung cancer
supporting_evidence: mass in the anterior thoracic wall
CT scan showing mass in the lingula extending into the mediastinum and thoracic wall
refuting_evidence: age is relatively young for typical lung cancer presentation
additional_information_needed: further imaging studies to assess for metastasis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Tuberculosis
additional_information_needed: biopsy of the mass for histology and culture

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lymphoma
supporting_evidence: mass in the anterior thoracic wall
refuting_evidence: no lymphadenopathy noted on physical examination

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pleurisy with secondary infection or abscess
refuting_evidence: mass extending into the mediastinum and thoracic wall is atypical for simple pleurisy
additional_information_needed: biopsy or aspiration of the mass
repeat imaging to assess for abscess formation

required.content: What management decisions were made for this patient?
required.response: A diagnostic procedure was performed, and cultures of blood and urine were obtained.

teaching_points.content: Diagnostic procedures and cultures are essential for identifying the underlying cause of complex presentations.
